headline: High: Perplexity can ingest uploaded PDFs from pdf.js, creating default-path data leakage and downstream citation-driven error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js is a browser-based PDF processor with no network egress, while Perplexity is a vendor-hosted search/RAG agent that can browse and ingest uploaded PDFs. The only clear bridge is manual transfer of PDF content, so prompt injection is possible but not automatic and the blast radius is limited to the transferred document.
conditions: IF a user copies PDF text from pdf.js into Perplexity prompts or uploads the same PDF to Perplexity
IF the PDF contains attacker-controlled instructions that Perplexity treats as prompt text
mitigations: Do not paste raw PDF text into Perplexity
Upload only sanitized excerpts
Add a human review step before acting on PDF-derived instructions
Use a separate workspace for untrusted PDFs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF documents locally and has no network egress, but Perplexity is vendor-hosted and explicitly accepts uploaded PDFs and images for analysis. If the same sensitive PDF is moved from pdf.js into Perplexity, document contents can leave the local environment and flow to a third-party backend in the default product path.
conditions: IF a PDF containing sensitive data is opened in pdf.js and then uploaded to Perplexity
IF Perplexity retains uploaded document content in its vendor backend
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive PDFs to Perplexity
Redact sensitive pages before upload
Use Perplexity only on non-sensitive documents
Confirm retention settings before upload
requires-engineering: route sensitive documents to a local-only RAG stack

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and file handling for PDFs, while Perplexity is session-scoped with shared state across sessions for the same user. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem write or git mutation, so direct resource conflict is limited; the main overlap is concurrent handling of the same documents or queries.
conditions: IF both agents are used concurrently on the same PDF corpus
IF Perplexity session state is reused across threads or Spaces for the same user
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same source PDF set
Use separate sessions per task
Keep one agent read-only for a given workflow
Rename or version documents before handoff

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system that produces cited answers from browsing context, and pdf.js can surface PDF content for human review. If a user treats pdf.js-extracted text as authoritative input to Perplexity, errors or omissions can cascade into cited but wrong answers; Perplexity’s browsing does not guarantee verification of the original PDF source.
conditions: IF text extracted or viewed in pdf.js is pasted into Perplexity as factual ground truth
IF Perplexity answers are used without checking the original PDF
mitigations: Verify claims against the original PDF
Ask Perplexity for source links before relying on an answer
Cross-check critical facts in a second source
Mark extracted text as untrusted until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js is open-source and local-browser oriented, while Perplexity is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and sends queries plus uploaded documents to its backend. That creates a compliance mismatch for regulated or residency-sensitive PDFs because the same document class can move from a local viewer into a third-party service without a documented residency guarantee in the profiles.
conditions: IF the PDF contains regulated data such as PHI, export-controlled data, or EU PII
IF the organization requires local-only processing or a specific residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of Perplexity
Use a local-only viewer and local-only search stack
Check vendor retention and residency terms before upload
Restrict uploads to non-regulated documents
requires-engineering: implement policy-based upload blocking
